rhesus macaque infected with a C5-tropic SHIV, SHIVSF162.P4, develop broad neutralizing antibody responses that are similar to those observed in HIV infected patients.

the development and characterization of broadly neutralizing anti-human immunodeficieny virus (anti-HIY) antibodies in macaques infected witli a CCR5 tropic simian/human immuno-deficiency virus (SHlV), SHIVSF 162P4.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the macaques infected by the CCR5-tropism SHIVSF162p3 developed broadly reactive neutralizing antibodies against HIV, which are similar in breadth to those observed in certain patients with HIV-1 infection.
SHIVSF162p4 is a useful model of HIV-1 infection, and the development of cross-reactive neutralization antibodies in some animals is a useful model for the study of HIV-1 neutralization.

the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies in macaques infected chronically with a CCR-5-tropic SHIV is a slow process, which may take up to 2 years, that requires continuous viral replication and that is not sufficient to protect against disease progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a CCR5 tropic SHIV (SF162P4) infection of macaques leads to the development of broadly neutralizing anti-HIV antibody responses.
the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV in macaques is a slow process and is dependent on the presence of viral replication for extended period of time.
the development of cross-reactive neutralization is not a sufficient condition for the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies, but it is a necessary condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the macaques we infected with SHIV developed antibodies that neutralize a wide variety of HIV-1 strains.
cross-reactive anti-human immunodeficienct virus (anti-HI) neutralizing antibodies are induced in a subset of macaques infected by the CCR5-tropisimian/human immunodeficience virus (SHIV).
cross-reactive anti HIV-1 neutralizing antibodies are not sufficient for controlling viral replication in the absence of other protective immune responses.
